title: 5. Complete Cross-Referencing System
use_cases: Use when tracking character appearances across complex narrative arcs
Implement when maintaining continuity for series bibles and worldbuilding
Configure when mapping specific locations to chronological scene events
Use when performing a reverse lookup to find all mentions of a specific clue or faction
Implement when managing large casts to prevent narrative inconsistencies
content:
Link every element of your story for total interconnectivity.

Connect characters to scenes, locations to events, and worldbuilding elements throughout your narrative. See at a glance which characters appear in each scene, which locations are referenced, and how your world elements tie into the plot. Everything is interconnected.

#### Cross-Reference Types

- Characters to Scenes: Track which characters appear where
- Locations to Scenes: Map where events take place
- World Elements to Scenes: Link factions, magic, technology to plot
- Visual Badge Selection: Easy multi-select interface
- Reverse Lookup: See all scenes featuring a character or location

#### Writer Benefits

- Never lose track of character appearances
- Ensure consistent location descriptions
- Track when worldbuilding elements are introduced
- Perfect for ensemble casts and complex worlds
- Ideal for mystery writers tracking clues and suspects
- Essential for series continuity across multiple books
